BiblicalUsage: Shot is the scourge, the lash, and it falls on the guilty and the innocent alike in this life. Job asks why the scourge slays suddenly and laughs at the trial of the innocent, Isaiah hears men boasting that the overflowing scourge will pass them by, Rehoboam threatens whips where his father used whips, and the proverb keeps a whip for the horse and a rod for the fool.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the scourge is a picture of judgment that no bargain can turn aside. The men in Isaiah made a covenant with death to escape it, and I hold that only the truth, not a lie, is a refuge.
